A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlashVGGT and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–C. Matching content across pagination changes supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 and Appendix B report original reconstruction experiments, accuracy and resource measurements, and ablations in Tables 1–10 and associated figures.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, downsampling comparisons, and component timing measurements in Appendix B, Tables 11–14.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same descriptor construction, auxiliary tokens, cross-attention, chunk-recursive memory updates, and two-stage training procedure. The newly evaluated downsampling variants are comparison controls.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds evaluation on in-the-wild photo-tourism imagery through IMC PhotoTourism, using sequences of 5–25 images (Table 11). Existing training datasets and the other evaluation datasets and tasks are retained.

E2.justification: New Table 13 evaluates three additional controls: input downsampling, DINO-feature downsampling, and a global-attention downsampling/upsampling bottleneck. Comparator membership in the retained experiments, including the Perceiver-style comparison, is unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 12 adds pose metrics at 5- and 10-degree thresholds on 10-frame RealEstate10K sequences, supplementing the retained 30-degree evaluation. Added experiments specify 5–25-frame PhotoTourism inputs, downsampling controls with the same training scheme and similar computational budgets, and component timing for 1,000-image sequences.

E4.justification: Table 13 adds a targeted analysis of where downsampling should occur, comparing descriptor compression with resizing inputs, encoded features, or all global-block tokens. Table 14 further examines the computational bottleneck through component timing. Existing ablations and sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The added tables continue point-estimate reporting; the existing model-confidence analysis is unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing tables and visual findings are unchanged; Tables 11–14 add focused benchmark, stricter-pose, control, and timing results. For example, PhotoTourism AUC@5 is 51.87 for FlashVGGT, 52.74 for VGGT, and 51.43 for FastVGGT. Table 13 reports Abs Rel of 0.161 for descriptor attention versus 0.241 for the global bottleneck. Table 14 reports total times of 35.37 and 377.60 seconds for FlashVGGT and VGGT. These are additional evaluations, not corrections to earlier scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, attention and memory equations (1–6), and computational-complexity arguments are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about compressed descriptor attention, chunk-recursive inference, competitive reconstruction accuracy, over 90% inference-time reduction for 1,000 images, and scaling beyond 3,000 views.

C2.justification: The new downsampling discussion attributes the controls' inferior reconstruction accuracy to loss of high-frequency details and explains the advantage of preserving full-resolution features and queries while compressing keys and values. Existing limitations concerning short sequences, deformation, lighting, and unexplored compression designs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 describes where each new control resizes its inputs or features, including the global bottleneck's subsequent upsampling. Existing implementation settings, training resources, and project-access information are unchanged. The new controls' precise downsampling factors are not supplied.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added: Dens3R, More, Radial Attention, Quest, and Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks. They extend the attention-efficiency context in Section 2 and the architecture-integration examples in Appendix C, without substantially changing the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds short Appendix B experiment descriptions and an acknowledgments section, updates the author/contact header, renames the descriptor-token paragraph heading, and corrects the top-kkk typo. The overall section organization and most existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 11–14 are added, and the final appendix page is reflowed, moving Section C into the right column. The author block and reference layout also change. Existing figures and tables retain their visual content and display structures.

improvement.justification: The added PhotoTourism and stricter-pose evaluations broaden validation, while the downsampling controls and component timing better support the design and efficiency rationale. The gains are limited: Table 13 shows better reconstruction accuracy at higher runtime and memory than its controls, and omits the evaluation dataset and precise downsampling factors. Overall, v2 provides useful additional evidence without resolving a major deficiency.
